texts.facts: Page No. 1 of 22 Bk Award 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the investigation by the police officials, an intimation was received by the police and as such concerned police official reached the place of accident on 08.02.2019, but no one was found there. During this, a call was received from Safderjung hospital and MLC of Anguri was collected. Thereafter statement of Rajesh, son of injured was recorded at his residence. It was stated that on 08.02.2019, he was driving his motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SDT-5508 and his mother was sitting as pillion rider. They were going from Chirag Delhi to Lajpat Nagar and as they reached at BRT road, a bus which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, hit his motorcycle from behind. Due to such impact, his mother/injured/Anguri fell down and got injury on her head. Further, it is Anguri Devi vs Dinesh Babu on 10 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185151479/ 1 submitted that as the bus got slowed down, he took picture of offending vehicle from his mobile phone and same is CH-01GA-5761. On the left side of bus, "police" is written. Thereafter, he took injured to Safderjung hospital in an auto. On the pointing out of complainant, site plan was prepared. Mechanical inspection of motorcycle of complainant was got inspected. 3. The police after investigation in present case filed charge sheet for offence u/s 279,338 IPC against the respondent/driver. Present DAR was also filed by the MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. Page No. 2 of 22 BK investigating officer. 4. Further, as per record, respondent no.1/driver, and Respondent no.2/owner appeared in present case. There is no insurance company as offending vehicle is government vehicle. Written statement filed by respondents. 5. As per the defence of R-1 & R-2, presence of the offending vehicle at the spot of accident and it is being driven by R-1 is not denied. But it is claimed that no accident is caused by such bus it is further stated that one old lady namely Anguri Devi fell down due to rash and negligent driving of Rajesh who was driving such motorcycle on which Anguri Devi was sitting. It is further statted that such accident was witnessed by the passeger of such bus. It is further stated that a judicial inquiry was conducted by the department of R-1 and copy of the same is placed on record and as per such inquiry no accident happened with the bus. 6. From the material on record, the following issues were framed on 29.05.2019 by my Ld. Predecessor: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 08.02.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no.CH-01 GA 5761 being driven by R1 and owned by R2? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 7. Injured/ Victim Smt. Anguri Devi filed her examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She relied upon various documents Ex. PW-1/1 to PW-1/4(colly) including MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. Page No. 3 of 22 BK OPD cards, DAR, MLC of concerned hospital and copy of Aadhar card. Such witness was cross-examined by learned counsel for R-1& R-2. 8. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. Anguri Devi vs Dinesh Babu on 10 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185151479/ 2 9. Respondent/driver filed his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit as Ex. R-1W-1/A. He relied upon document as Ex.R-1W-1/A. He was cross-examined by counsel for claimant/petitioner. Further, Sh. Satya Pal was also examined as eye witness as R-1W-2/1. He was also cross-examined by learned counsel for petitioner. Further, learned counsel for claimant also filed written arguments in prescribed form. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. Page No. 4 of 22 BK Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 13. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 23. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. Page No . 8 of 22 BK (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability 23.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), Anguri Devi vs Dinesh Babu on 10 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185151479/ 5 (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 23.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 23.7. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Anguri Devi vs Dinesh Babu on 10 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185151479/ 8 Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. 31. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.1,05,000/- with simple interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till its actual realization. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 37. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. However, in such cases, the Tribunal shall MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. Page No. 16 of 22 BK make sure that the amount is actually spent for the purpose and the demand is not a ruse to withdraw money. In the case of semi-illiterate claimants, the Tribunal Anguri Devi vs Dinesh Babu on 10 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185151479/ 10 should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. In the case of literate persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. 38. In this background of legal position, it may be noted MACT No. 320/19 Anguri Devi v. Dinesh Babu & Ors. Page No. 18 of 22 BK that in present case, accused suffered injury and incurred expenses including on medical expenses, special diet, conveyance. 40. The following conditions are to be adhered to by SBI, Saket Courts, Delhi with respect to the fixed deposits:- (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
